items.stem: Why is implementing IHostedService / BackgroundService preferred over starting a bare background thread?

options.text: Its lifetime is coordinated with the host so it can run graceful shutdown and cleanup
options.rationale: Correct: hosted services get start/stop hooks tied to the host lifetime for graceful shutdown.

options.text: It makes the work run on the UI thread
options.rationale: Background services are not about UI threads; .NET workers are typically headless.

options.text: It guarantees the work never fails
options.rationale: Nothing guarantees failure-free execution; resilience must be designed in.

options.text: It removes the need for dependency injection
options.rationale: Hosted services integrate with DI rather than removing it.

items.explanation: Correct: hosted services get start/stop hooks tied to the host lifetime for graceful shutdown.

items.stem: Queues used by your background tasks guarantee at-least-once delivery. Select TWO measures that keep processing correct under duplicates and restarts.

options.rationale: Correct: idempotent handlers tolerate the same message being processed more than once.

options.text: Use checkpoints so a restarted task resumes from its last known point
options.rationale: Correct: checkpoints let long tasks resume instead of restarting from the beginning.

options.text: Assume each message is delivered exactly once
options.rationale: At-least-once delivery means duplicates are possible; assuming exactly-once is unsafe.

options.text: Delete the message before processing completes
options.rationale: Deleting before completion can lose work if processing then fails.

options.text: Store large sensitive payloads inside each message
options.rationale: Sensitive data in payloads risks exposure via logs or dead-letters; pass a reference instead.

items.explanation: Correct: idempotent handlers tolerate the same message being processed more than once.

items.stem: A message fails on every attempt because its referenced record no longer exists. What should the processor do?

options.text: Treat it as a permanent failure and move it to a dead-letter queue
options.rationale: Correct: permanent failures should be dead-lettered rather than retried forever.

options.text: Retry it indefinitely until it succeeds
options.rationale: Endless retries of a permanent failure block the queue and waste attempts.

options.text: Silently drop it with no record
options.rationale: Silently dropping loses the ability to investigate; dead-lettering preserves it.

options.text: Pause all other processing until it succeeds
options.rationale: A single poison message should not halt the whole pipeline.

items.explanation: Correct: permanent failures should be dead-lettered rather than retried forever.
